messages:
mira: Heads-up — nightly eval spike on rdw-v2-13b-q6 for nightly-legal-qa. Hallucination rate 1.2% -> 6.9%, failing 82/500 prompts. Anyone touch quant profiles or detokenizer recently? :rotating_light:

alex: Saw the alert. I didn't change quant profiles. There was a runtime deploy at 03:12 UTC (infra-bot) for a KV cache write-lock fix. Could be related to continuous batching/kv interaction. pinging @kim and @raj. :eyes:

eval-bot: Automated summary:
Model: rdw-v2-13b-q6
Eval: nightly-legal-qa-v2
Window: 2026-03-10T03:00Z -> 2026-03-10T03:30Z
Metric delta: hallucination_rate 0.012 -> 0.069
Failed prompts: 82 / 500
Top failing example (prompt id 4231):
```
Prompt: "Does statute 17A apply to X when ..."
Gen: "Yes, under statute 17A the defendant must... [fabricated statute text referencing 'section 5B']"
Ref: "No relevant statute — answer should be 'No, statute 17A is not applicable in this context.'"
```

kim: I started a local repro. Reproduced the bad generation with seed=42 using the q6 runtime binary. Repro command below — identical hallucinated output. Hypothesis: the q6 kernel selector may be choosing a fallback attention implementation that mishandles long prefix offsets (KV pointers off by one) when kv_cache is enabled. Haven't confirmed yet.

raj: Can you paste the exact reproduce command and the minimal prompt file? I'll try on a different machine and also test with kv_cache disabled.

kim: Repro command:
```
python reproduce.py --model rdw-v2-13b-q6 --prompts tests/legal/4231.json --seed 42 --quant q6 --kv-cache=true --max-len 512
```
Prompt file is attached to the issue I'm about to open (see below). With `--kv-cache=false` the hallucination goes down to baseline (~1.3%).

alex: Interesting — that aligns with the runtime change at 03:12 where we relaxed kv_cache_write_lock to reduce contention for high-throughput batching. If kv writes can race, stale prefixes could be served to the next request in the same batch. I'm rolling the runtime change back on a canary now to confirm. If rollback fixes it we'll do a hotfix.

mira: I'll open a regression issue and add the 82 failing prompts to a new regression promptset. Tagging QA and oncall in the issue. Can we also pin Hosted canary to the int4 variant until we have confidence?

raj: On it — creating a canary route: 5% -> rdw-v2-13b-int4, 95% -> rdw-v2-13b-q6 with fallback to host-v2 if hallucination_rate > 3% for a 5m window. Adding alert: `eval.hallucination_rate > 0.03` for nightly-legal-qa. I'll post the canary config in the issue. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks. Next steps: (1) confirm rollback result, (2) add failing prompts to regression set + add unit test, (3) run a quant-kernel unit test sweep for q6 attention offsets. I'll own the issue and follow up with a postmortem if it's a kernel bug.

alex: If rollback fixes, we should also run a small AB test of the kv_lock variant under load to reproduce the race. Also check detokenizer changes from last month just in case.

kim: Will run kernel diagnostics and dump KV pointers for the failing sequence. Posting logs to the issue shortly.
